description: Jordan is holding a hand-stitched quilt inherited from their grandmother and must decide who will keep it, how it may be displayed, where it will go, and how long it can be lent within the family.

shared_context.S1: The quilt is a hand-stitched family heirloom measuring about 190 centimeters by 210 centimeters.
shared_context.S2: Jordan has been keeping the quilt and will make the final plan for its care and family use.
shared_context.S3: The quilt can be displayed or lent, but the family wants to avoid treating it as an ordinary picnic blanket.
shared_context.S4: At family keepsake check-ins, each person gives Jordan one practical update before Jordan settles the plan.
shared_context.S5: The family reunion is six weeks away, and several relatives hope the quilt can be seen there.

PF1.text: Maya found a handwritten note from Grandma saying that Lena should be the quilt's keeper; Maya has not shown the note to the family yet.

PF2.text: Ravi spoke with a textile conservator at the local museum, who recommended no washing, flat display only, and rolled storage with acid-free tissue rather than folding; he has not passed that recommendation along yet.

PF3.text: Elena measured the possible walls: the north hallway has 210 centimeters of clear width and no direct sunlight, while the sunroom is too bright and the living-room wall is only 180 centimeters wide; she has not shared the measurements yet.

PF4.text: Theo learned from Lena that she can accept the quilt only as a 90-day family loan, after which it must return to Jordan; Lena told Theo this privately and has not told Jordan.

acceptance_conditions: Lena must be named as the quilt's keeper or as the primary recipient of the family loan honoring Grandma's note.
The quilt must be displayed flat rather than used as a blanket.
The quilt must be stored rolled with acid-free tissue.
The display location must be the north hallway.
The loan duration must be exactly 90 days.
The settlement must include a commitment stating that the quilt returns to Jordan after the 90-day loan.
Maya's note must be cited as justification for naming Lena as keeper or primary loan recipient.

content_checks.C1: (("Lena" in decisions['keeper']) and (("keeper" in decisions['keeper']) or ("custodian" in decisions['keeper']) or (decisions['keeper'] == "Lena"))) or any((c['target'] == 'Lena') and ('loan' in c['type'] or 'Loan' in c['type']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C2: "flat display" in decisions['display_method'] or "Flat display" in decisions['display_method']
content_checks.C3: "rolled" in decisions['storage_method'] and "acid-free" in decisions['storage_method'] and "tissue" in decisions['storage_method']
content_checks.C4: "north hallway" in decisions['display_location'] or "North hallway" in decisions['display_location']
content_checks.C6: any((('Jordan' in c['detail']) or ('jordan' in c['detail'])) and (('return' in c['detail']) or ('Return' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Grandma's note changes the plan by requiring Lena to be named as keeper or as the primary loan recipient, rather than leaving Jordan as the only named holder without a Lena-specific arrangement.
The conservator's recommendation changes the display method to flat display and the storage method to rolled storage with acid-free tissue instead of ordinary folding or washing.
The measurements change the location choice to the north hallway because its exact 210-centimeter width fits the 190-centimeter quilt and its lack of direct sunlight protects it.
Lena's private acceptance changes the loan duration to exactly 90 days and requires a commitment stating that the quilt returns to Jordan afterward.
